policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Much every way: first of all, that they were intrusted with the oracles of God' renders no connective at all for this position; a postpositive gar and its omission are alike invisible in the English, and no note is mapped here.
kathos and kathaper are synonyms both rendered 'as it is written'; the ASV wording cannot separate them and the only notes here are a greek_gloss on 'God forbid' and an OT citation.

'And mightest prevail' stands in a single hopos purpose clause with 'that thou mightest be justified'; ASV renders the whole clause as purpose whether the verb is future indicative nikeseis or aorist subjunctive nikeses, so the English does not distinguish the two.
ASV text reads 'But if the truth of God ...' (de), and the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read For.' places gar in the margin, so the base de is the reading rendered.
The article on the substantival participle has no English exponent; 'There is none that understandeth' is the same rendering with or without ho, and no note is mapped here.
As with the preceding participle, 'There is none that seeketh after God' renders the substantival participle identically whether or not the article is present; nothing in the ASV distinguishes them.
'There is none that doeth good' shows no trace of an added article before the participle; article presence or absence is not rendered in English and no note is mapped to this verse.

ASV text reads only 'unto all them that believe', and the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities add and upon all.' consigns kai epi pantas to the margin, so the shorter base reading is the one rendered.

'through faith' is the ASV rendering of dia pisteos with or without the article tes; the only note here is an alternative_rendering on 'propitiation', which is about English wording and cannot decide a reading.

The Greek article is not separately rendered in 'for the showing, I say, of his righteousness'; its presence or absence leaves the English unchanged, and the notes here are cross references, a greek_gloss, and an alternative_rendering, none of which is a textual_variant.
ASV text reads 'We reckon therefore' (oun), and the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read For we reckon.' puts gar in the margin, so the ASV rendered oun, not the base gar.

The variant is only the order of dikaiousthai and pistei; both yield 'is justified by faith' in English, and the mapped textual_variant note concerns the connective 'For we reckon', not this word order.

ASV 'is he not the God of Gentiles also?' carries no connective, but the ASV routinely leaves a postpositive de untranslated in a question sequence, so its absence in English does not exclude the added particle; no note is mapped here.

ASV renders 'if so be that God is one', a conditional clause matching eiper; epeiper is causal ('since indeed') and would have produced 'seeing that/since', so the ASV wording distinguishes the base reading.
histanomen and histomen are alternative present forms of the same verb with the same sense, both rendered 'we establish'; the notes here are all alternative_rendering and cannot decide a reading.
